evidence: LY skew first-two operations reduce to one alternating form in dimension two
Matrix conjugacy and centralizer counts, and independent F3,F5,F7 exhaustive algebraic condition enumeration
correctness.rationale: On any two-dimensional vector space, the skew binary bracket has [x,y]=omega(x,y)b and any trilinear operation alternating in its first two entries has {x,y,z}=omega(x,y)A(z). For char K!=2, every nontrivial involution E diagonalizes as diag(1,-1), so each eigenspace is a one-dimensional LY subalgebra and the binary/ternary product Nijenhuis defects vanish on the two basis generators. For J^2=-I, scalar J is automatically Nijenhuis; any non-scalar J admits a basis (v,Jv), in which its matrix is the standard complex form. Direct substitution of that form into the binary and ternary identities makes all defects vanish regardless of b,A. Over finite odd q, ordered distinct eigenlines give q(q+1) E; J conjugacy classes give q(q-1) if -1 nonsquare or q(q+1)+2 if square. Each fixed E admits q-1 anticommuting J with bc=-1, so q(q^2-1) compatible pairs, and over F_(q^m) the geometric count is q^(3m)-q^m, giving zeta (1-qT)/(1-q^3T). Independent matrix enumeration over F3,F5,F7 yielded (12,6,24),(30,32,120),(56,42,336). No characteristic-two assertion.
residual_risks: Algebraic complex structure outside R means J^2=-I plus the specified polynomial Nijenhuis identities, not a complex manifold structure.
